column1: # Tripwire table (ADR 0017): sink signatures for every language.
# One row per signature: <kind> TAB <signature> TAB <fixture line>.
# kind is a planner sink kind: sql, nosql, shell, code_eval, deserialize,
# file, http_client or template. A signature is a plain byte
# string of 2 to 64 bytes, matched case-sensitively on each line of the
# redacted file, comments and strings included. A signature that starts
# with an identifier byte (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, _) must not follow one, so
# "open(" does not match "fopen(". A signature ending in "(" after an
# identifier byte also matches with spaces or tabs before the "(", so
# "exec(" matches "exec (cmd)". The fixture line must match its row
# (tripwire_test.go). A hit is a candidate for the reader, never a finding.
# Known gaps, left to discovery: Ruby and Perl backtick commands (a
# backtick row would hit every JavaScript template literal and Markdown
# code span); calls of a bare name imported from elsewhere ("from
# subprocess import run", then "run(cmd)"; the import line is the hit);
# calls split across lines; Swift Process and NSTask (the names are too
# common to match alone); string-interpolated SQL literals with no call
# name (Scala sql"...", Kotlin and Groovy GString queries).
# Objects decoded from bytes or text
# Files opened, read, written or served by path
# Common spellings the first review found missing
# Process, SQL and eval APIs from the second review sweep
